correctness.rationale: For every finite abelian group A of order \(n\ge5\), the graph has exactly three families of n disjoint n-point clique lines and precisely \((|A[2]|-1)n^2/4\) off-line four-cliques. The normalized off-line triangle admits a fourth neighbor if and only if its group difference has order two; no fifth neighbor exists. Exact Euler counting gives \((n-1)^3-I\). The published Latin-square-graph homology-concentration theorem (arXiv:2606.27328, Theorem 3.12) identifies this Euler characteristic with the entire degree-two Betti number. For any nontrivial translation every vertex orbit has the same length d, and each invariant union of q orbits contributes sign \((-1)^{q-1}\) to ordinary Lefschetz. Nonline invariant four-cliques occur only for line translations of order two and have exact multiplicity \(n^2/4\) and sign -1. Subtracting reduced augmentation produces all claimed character cases; rational averaging yields every subgroup quotient. The included direct enumeration tests every translation in seven groups, 1149 distinct subgroup quotient ranks, and two complete GF2 simplicial homology computations. These experiments corroborate, but do not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A full translation-group representation for all abelian group-table Latin-square graphs is a natural infinite-family symmetry classification whose involution correction has structural meaning from intercalate face orbits. It yields exact rational homology for every translation subgroup quotient rather than another nonequivariant Betti number. The sharp full-quotient criterion \(\dim H_2=|A|-|A[2]|\) distinguishes all three abelian group structures at order eight, and identifies an infinite family of nontrivial rationally acyclic geometric quotients. These are motivated invariants not determined by the source homology ranks; neither arbitrary finite cutoffs nor routine parameter substitutions.
